title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: GOAL’s ICSP Programme in Zimbabwe is ensuring that vulnerable communities (including people with disabilities) facing poverty and exclusion are overcoming crises and achieving greater resilience and wellbeing in Matabeleland South Province through improving public health services, livelihoods, food and nutrition security. In 2024, 27,060 individuals were reached through ICSP in Bulilima and Mangwe districts. These districts are characterised by high levels of food insecurity, poor infrastructure and are adversely affected by disasters. Through ICSP, there has been improved access to safe and clean water through the rehabilitation of water points coupled with capacity building of Sanitation Action Groups (SAGs) and Health Clubs to foster sustainability. Internal Savings and Lending (ISAL) groups have been strengthened through Business Development Trainings and linking them to Formal Financial Institutions thereby increasing household incomes. Communities have also received Crops and Livestock Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) technologies trainings and awareness sessions/capacity building on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) contingency plans on Early Warning Systems. The programme has a Nutrition Social Behaviour Change (SBC) component, the Food and Nutrition Security-Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (FNS-NIPP) approach aimed at improving consumption of diversified diets through promotion of better nutrition practices amongst communities. Our ICSP interventions are nested within a SBC approach, such as Gender Action Learning Systems (GALS - a community-led methodology that uses visual diagrams to empower women and men to imagine the futures they want by taking action against societal norms that drive gender inequality).. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 3: People Have Food & Nutrition Security. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: The programme supports the development of contingency plans and the operation of Early Warning Systems for shocks that impact food and nutrition security (including droughts).
